caution: Lye (sodium/potassium hydroxide) is caustic. It burns skin and eyes on contact and releases irritating fumes when dissolved. Handle only with eye protection, gloves, and ventilation.

claims.claim: Soap is formed by saponification: a fat or oil reacts with an alkali (lye) to split into soap and glycerol.
claims.source: General chemistry — saponification is a standard reaction documented across independent chemistry references. BOOK_FILE not provided; this claim does not derive from any book text.

claims.claim: Before manufactured lye existed, people commonly made an alkaline lye solution by leaching wood ash with water.
claims.source: General historical-chemistry knowledge (potash/lye production from wood ash), independently documented across multiple traditional-craft and chemistry-history references, not book-derived.

claims.claim: Rendered animal fat (tallow), especially from cattle or sheep, was one of the most common traditional soap-making fats because it was a byproduct already available after butchering.
claims.source: General historical-craft knowledge on traditional soap-making fats; independently documented, not book-derived.

claims.claim: Without lab equipment, the strength of a wood-ash lye solution was traditionally estimated with a simple buoyancy test, such as checking whether a fresh egg or small potato floats at the right level in the liquid.
claims.source: General historical-craft knowledge (folk lye-testing methods); independently documented across traditional soap-making references, not book-derived.

claims.claim: Making soap means combining melted fat with a lye solution and stirring until the mixture thickens to "trace," the point at which saponification has progressed enough for the mixture to hold its shape.
claims.source: General chemistry/craft knowledge on the saponification process; independently documented, not book-derived.

claims.claim: Because raw lye is caustic and can cause serious chemical burns, it must be handled with eye protection, gloves, and ventilation, with any splash rinsed immediately with plenty of water.
claims.source: General chemical-safety knowledge for handling caustic alkalis (sodium/potassium hydroxide); independently documented, not book-derived.
